buyer_persona: First-time US food-truck operator, pre-launch, aspiring owner-operator with a concept but no filed permits yet.
changelog: 1.0: Initial release with guide, 5-sheet workbook, and 4 document templates.
disclaimer: This kit is planning information, not legal/tax advice; verify every fee and form with the issuing agency. All cost figures are illustrative ranges only, never current facts. No outcome promises are made.

faq.a: Most first-time stacks fall in the 5 to 12 range, but your count is the yes rows on your map after agency verification. Do not rely on another operator count from a different jurisdiction.
faq.q: How many permits will I need?

faq.a: Build the estimator, verify every fee with the issuing agency, and sum verified figures. Illustrative ranges teach structure only and must never be used for paying.
Planning context is 4 to 10 weeks, but your timeline depends on backlogs, slots, completeness, and readiness. Build the critical path from quoted lead times plus buffer.
Often yes for vendor permits while health approval may sit at county level. Confirm city by city and keep each city as separate rows.
faq.q: Do I need a separate permit for each city?

how_to_use: Record your jurisdictions and concept, build the permit map item by item with agency verification, build the estimator with illustrative ranges then verified fees, run the dependency-ordered sequence with the tracker, prepare for inspection with the checklist, and seed the renewal calendar with alert-date formulas on approval day.
limitations: Planning structure only; does not state required permits, fees, forms, or lead times. Those come only from issuing agencies and change. Illustrative ranges are teaching material only. No legal or tax advice. No assurance of approval, inspection passage, or launch date. Each added city or menu category adds complexity kept as separate rows.
long_description: A planning system for the fragmented 5 to 12 item permit stack: jurisdiction map, cost and timeline estimator with sum formulas, dependency-ordered sequence from entity through certifications, commissary, inspections, and vendor permit, plus a daily application tracker, an inspection-day checklist, and a renewal calendar with alert-date formulas. Guide includes verification discipline, checklists, illustrative examples labeled illustrative, FAQ, limitations, and disclosure.
name: Food Truck Permit Navigator
outcome_statement: Maintain a verified map of what applies, an estimator grounded in confirmed fees, filings run in dependency order with dated tracking, inspection readiness, and renewals flagged before expiration.
problem_statement: A fragmented 5 to 12 permit stack across unconnected agencies, fee totals in the low thousands, 4 to 10 week timelines, missing items that delay launch, and expirations that can shut a truck down.
short_description: Permit map, cost and timeline estimator, application tracker, renewal calendar, and inspection checklist for first-time operators.
support: Included: planning and routine instructions in the guide. Not included: legal or tax advice, agency filings, or fee confirmations. Verify every fee and form with the issuing agency.
whats_included: workbook with 5 sheets: permit register with cost formulas, timeline planner, application tracker, renewal calendar with alert-date formulas, inspection checklist
4 docx templates: agency contact sheet, document packet checklist, commissary comparison sheet, renewal reminder setup guide
who_for: First-time US food-truck operators, pre-launch, who need an organized path through entity, certifications, commissary, inspections, and vendor permits.
who_not_for: Operators seeking legal or tax advice, current fee schedules, or assured approvals, or established fleets needing multi-unit management software.
